description: A Developer Productivity Lead must approve the retirement plan for a legacy artifact registry, deciding the shutdown mode, temporary compatibility access, customer archive access, and registry-log handling after the routine platform review.

shared_context.S1: The legacy artifact registry is scheduled for retirement on July 31.
shared_context.S2: Riley owns the final approval of the retirement plan.
shared_context.S3: The replacement registry has passed the standard migration tests, and the draft plan calls for shutting off the legacy registry's read and write access on July 31.
shared_context.S4: The standard retirement review requires sign-off from build compatibility, customer artifact access, and registry-log handling; each function owner gives a recommendation and Riley may approve once the required plan revisions are written down, without waiting for further investigation results.

PF1.text: While tracing an unrelated build failure this morning, Maya found that six active release branches still fetch packages by legacy-registry coordinates: payments-v3, mobile-android-2025.06, mobile-ios-2025.06, desktop-4.8, analytics-2.3, and edge-agent-1.9. A July 31 hard shutdown would break those branches, so they need read-only compatibility access until their releases complete; she has not updated the retirement ticket yet.

PF2.text: Jonah confirmed with the account team today that Harbor Health's contract requires downloadable access to its registry artifacts for 730 days after registry retirement. The contract was found during a customer-renewal review and has not yet been attached to the platform ticket.

PF3.text: During a privacy review of registry telemetry this afternoon, Leila confirmed that access logs retain bearer-token fragments and therefore must have token fragments redacted and be purged after exactly 14 days, rather than the draft plan's 90-day retention; she has not opened the privacy finding yet.

acceptance_conditions: The legacy registry must use read-only compatibility access rather than a hard shutdown.
The read-only compatibility allowlist must include all six branch entries identified by build systems; additional entries are permitted.
Harbor Health must receive downloadable artifact access for exactly 730 days after retirement.
A commitment must record Harbor Health's 730-day downloadable archive access.
Registry access logs must be retained for exactly 14 days.
Bearer-token fragments in registry access logs must be redacted.
A commitment must explicitly record read-only compatibility access for the six active release branches.

content_checks.C2: 'payments-v3' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist'] and 'mobile-android-2025.06' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist'] and 'mobile-ios-2025.06' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist'] and 'desktop-4.8' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist'] and 'analytics-2.3' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist'] and 'edge-agent-1.9' in decisions['legacy_read_allowlist']
content_checks.C4: any('Harbor Health' in c['detail'] and '730' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('read-only' in c['detail'] and ('six' in c['detail'] or all(x in c['detail'] for x in ['payments-v3', 'mobile-android-2025.06', 'mobile-ios-2025.06', 'desktop-4.8', 'analytics-2.3', 'edge-agent-1.9'])) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The six named release branches change the retirement mode from a hard shutdown to read-only compatibility, supply the six required allowlist entries, and require a commitment documenting read-only access for those branches.
Harbor Health's contract changes the archive-access duration to exactly 730 days and requires a commitment whose detail names Harbor Health and the 730-day period.
The bearer-token fragments change log handling from the draft's 90-day retention to exactly 14 days and require token-fragment redaction.
